title: Define typed DataInitConfig for shared DataInit helpers
description:
Background: Tests currently need a typed config to replace large po::variables_map setup, but the shared helper builders live in pgb.
Motivation: Keep the config surface narrow so the helper umbrella can stay focused on the reusable builders.
Goal: Define the typed DataInitConfig and its defaults or shape only, without taking ownership of the helper-builder layer itself.
Research: This bead is the config companion to pgb, not a duplicate of it.

title: Test PrimeDoesNotOverfill
description:
Background: The ring-slot controller proposal includes a prime step that should stop at numActiveBuffers - 1.
Motivation: If priming can overfill, later advance logic can consume stale or nonexistent slots.
Goal: Add a unit test that proves repeated priming never creates more available slots than the ring can hold.
Research: The investigation note lists PrimeDoesNotOverfill as a core state-machine case for the extracted controller.

title: Extract HIP-free ring slot controller and state-machine tests
description:
Background: Ring arithmetic, availability, and barrier state are embedded in DataInitialization today.
Motivation: The slot state machine should be testable without GPU resources, and xmn is a duplicate of this owner.
Goal: Pull out a small HIP-free controller and add unit coverage for PrimeDoesNotOverfill, AdvanceConsumesAvailableSlot, AdvanceWrapsModuloActiveBufferCount, AdvanceMarksCopyBarrierRequired, MarkBarrierWaitedClearsBarrier, and CancelResetsToSlotZero.
Research: This bead owns the controller umbrella and the six named state-machine tests beneath it.

title: Document the second beginAsyncReset call as the triple-buffer case
description:
Background: main.cpp calls beginAsyncReset twice in sequence, but the second call is a no-op in double-buffer mode.
Motivation: The call site is hard to read until the buffer-depth policy is known from elsewhere.
Goal: Add a comment or equivalent clarification that the second call exists for the triple-buffer case and is intentionally harmless in double-buffer mode.
Research: The branch review notes that the second call becomes meaningful again once the buffer-depth inversion is fixed.

title: Introduce a HIP copy and event abstraction with RAII
description:
Background: DataInitialization directly manages streams, events, copies, synchronization, and pinned memory lifetimes.
Motivation: Behavior tests currently need real HIP even when they only care about ordering and submission, not device work.
Goal: Wrap memcpy, event, wait, and sync operations behind a narrow engine interface and give streams, events, and pinned staging memory RAII wrappers.
Research: The refactor note calls out HipCopyEngine plus a RecordingCopyEngine test double as the intended seam.

title: Coordinate the shared client GPU test target for data-init regressions
description:
Background: The GPU regression coverage should live behind one harness-facing target, not be scattered across multiple target definitions.
Motivation: A single shared target makes the data-init and ring-buffer tests easier to extend without repeating long source lists.
Goal: Keep this bead focused on CMake target organization only, whether by adding a dedicated client GPU test target or folding the cases into an existing batch-pointer target.
Research: This is harness work only; the concrete helper and test beads own the behavior.

title: Use multiplyElementSize consistently in copy helpers
description:
Background: One copy path computes bytes as elementBytes() times maxElements directly instead of using multiplyElementSize like the other paths.
Motivation: The inconsistency makes the byte-count logic harder to audit for narrow or sub-byte element types.
Goal: Route the copy-size calculation through the shared helper so all copy paths use the same sizing rule.
Research: The branch review calls out this inconsistency as a low-priority cleanup item.

title: Test NoBenchmarkPathSubmitsTwoRingResets
description:
Background: The missing production regression guard is the no-benchmark path that should submit two ring resets after warmup.
Motivation: Direct DataInitialization tests can prime the ring manually, but they do not prove the scheduler in main.cpp actually calls the reset hook.
Goal: Add a spy-based test that verifies the no-benchmark path submits two resets for the active problem.
Research: The investigation note proposes a RingResetSink-style seam specifically for this case.

title: Extract batch pointer layout computation
description:
Background: initializeGPUBatchedInputs mixes offset calculation, bounds checking, sparse metadata handling, pinned staging mutation, and HIP upload.
Motivation: Stale batch-pointer bugs are hard to test because the calculation and the upload are inseparable.
Goal: Pull the offset computation into a pure BatchPointerLayout helper and keep the uploader focused on transfer only.
Research: The refactor note says this would let the stale-pointer cases be tested without a GPU.

title: Fix pinned batch staging aliasing across async DMAs
description:
Background: The branch review found that m_pinnedBatchStaging is reused across per-tensor async batch-pointer uploads in initGPUBatchedInputs.
Motivation: hipMemcpyAsync can outlive the call site, so a later tensor can overwrite staging bytes before an earlier DMA consumes them.
Goal: Give each tensor its own staging slice or an equivalent striped buffer so the async copies never alias.
Research: The review calls this a confirmed data race and recommends a numTensors x m_maxBatch layout.

title: Test ValidationOnlyConfigurationUsesThreeSlots
description:
Background: Validation-only runs can still drive the solution loop even when timed benchmark enqueues are absent.
Motivation: Those runs are the cases where the deeper triple-buffer pipeline is supposed to be useful.
Goal: Add a test that proves the validation-only configuration uses three active ring slots.
Research: Proposal 2 says validation-driven untimed runs should be able to use the ring when they drive the loop.

title: Test AdvanceMarksCopyBarrierRequired
description:
Background: After the active slot advances, the compute side must wait for the corresponding copy-done event.
Motivation: Missing the barrier leaves the compute stream free to read a slot before its copy finishes.
Goal: Add a unit test that proves advance sets the barrier-needed state.
Research: The proposed controller coverage includes AdvanceMarksCopyBarrierRequired as the barrier transition.

title: Test ProblemDependentDataDoesNotFastPath
description:
Background: Problem-dependent input data should not use the same cached-ring shortcut as invariant input data.
Motivation: If problem-dependent inputs hit the fast path, the client can reuse stale data across problems.
Goal: Add a negative test for the problem-dependent init modes that proves the ring fast path stays disabled.
Research: The test investigation names problem-dependent data as a required guard for ring eligibility.

title: Rename misleading stream and ring-state names
description:
Background: The design note says several stream and ring state names do not match their real contract.
Motivation: asyncStream sometimes means target stream and sometimes means caller owns synchronization, while the ring flags hide the actual invariant they represent.
Goal: Rename the stream-selector parameters and ring-state fields so the names match the behavior: targetStream, callerOwnsCopySync, m_computeNeedsCopyBarrier, m_availableSlots, and m_altSlotsReady.
Research: The note specifically calls out copyInputs, resetOutput, initializeGPUBatchedInputs, copyValidToGPUBuffer, m_activeNeedsSync, m_pendingResets, and m_ringBufferWarm.

title: Add HipStreamGuard RAII helper
description:
Background: The GPU integration tests need a tiny wrapper around hipStreamCreate and hipStreamDestroy.
Motivation: Stream cleanup should not be spread across assertions and early returns in each test body.
Goal: Add a guard object that owns a HIP stream for the lifetime of the test scope.
Research: The test plan names HipStreamGuard as part of the shared fixture layer for the DataInit regression tests.

title: Move inline DataInitialization lifecycle methods out of the header
description:
Background: beginAsyncReset, cancelAsyncReset, advanceBuffer, and waitCopyDone are defined inline in the header even though they are not trivial accessors.
Motivation: The header is already dense, and the lifecycle logic is easier to review when it lives in the implementation file.
Goal: Move the non-hot lifecycle methods into the .cpp and keep the header focused on declarations.
Research: The review lists inline lifetime methods in the header as a minor cleanup item.

title: Reset outputs on the warm ring path when validation is enabled
description:
Background: The warm-path output reset is the validation-sensitive side of the sah policy.
Motivation: When validation is enabled, reuse must reset outputs in the target slot before the copy-done event; otherwise the warm ring can carry stale state forward.
Goal: Use SlotGuard plus resetOutput on the target slot before recording the copy-done event, and gate the D2D warm reset on m_keepPristineCopyOnGPU.
Research: This is the canonical warm-path output-reset bead; je3 and hgk inherit this policy.

title: Coordinate negative ringEligible guards
description:
Background: Not every configuration should be allowed to use the ring fast path under the sah policy.
Motivation: The expensive cases are the ones where eligibility drifts silently, so a compact negative suite is enough.
Goal: Cover the bounds-check and problem-dependent input modes that must not prime the ring, and keep benchmark-path reset-hook coverage in ve2.
Research: This bead is the negative-eligibility umbrella aligned to sah, not a competing implementation bead.

title: Extract a testable run scheduler from main.cpp
description:
Background: main.cpp currently owns problem setup, cancel/reset sequencing, wait barriers, warmups, benchmarks, validation, and async reset submission in one nested loop.
Motivation: That makes it hard to test the production ring-reset schedule without running the whole client on GPU hardware.
Goal: Move the sequencing into a scheduler or executor so the no-benchmark reset path can be verified with fakes or spies.
Research: The maintainability note suggests a SolutionRunExecutor or ClientRunScheduler and lists the ordering checks it should enable.

title: Rename the async-reset timing label
description:
Background: The ScopedTimer label async_reset_batchedinit fires only on the first slow-path batched-init call for a problem.
Motivation: The current label makes performance traces harder to interpret because it sounds like a true async-reset phase.
Goal: Rename the timing label to match the actual work being measured.
Research: The branch review calls this a small readability fix for timing analysis.

title: Add buildRingArgs shared test helper
description:
Background: The test plan wants a helper that turns the base DataInit arguments into a no-benchmark ring configuration.
Motivation: Ring tests should not hand-edit the benchmark counters and validation fields in every file.
Goal: Add a helper that sets the no-benchmark counts, validation mode, and any init overrides needed for ring behavior tests.
Research: The investigation note gives buildRingArgs as the canonical setup for the ring-buffer regression cases.

title: Extract output-reset planning from copy mechanics
description:
Background: Output reset behavior is spread across prepareGPUInputsInternal, beginAsyncReset, fillSlot, and resetOutput.
Motivation: The policy for when outputs need reset is hidden inside copy code, which makes the ring-buffer behavior hard to reason about.
Goal: Create an OutputResetPlanner or OutputInitializationPolicy that decides whether a slot needs no reset, reset-from-valid, or full fill.
Research: The design note says that planner should be shared by both the normal fast path and the ring-buffer paths.

title: Test TimedBenchmarkConfigurationDoesNotAllocateAltSlotsOrAdvanceRing
description:
Background: Proposal 2 says timed benchmark enqueues should not allocate or consume the ring.
Motivation: Benchmark runs should not pay for extra ring buffers or background reset work that they never use.
Goal: Add a test for nonzero benchmark counters that proves alt slots are not allocated and the ring does not advance.
Research: The proposal’s mode table states that timed benchmark enqueues should run with the ring disabled.

title: Make DataInitialization lifecycle explicit
description:
Background: DataInitialization is both a listener and a directly called input service, so state changes are split across preProblem, preSolution, cancelAsyncReset, prepareGPUInputs, waitCopyDone, and beginAsyncReset.
Motivation: Correctness depends on call-site discipline that is hard to test and easy to break.
Goal: Add explicit lifecycle methods such as beginProblem, beginSolution, primeNextInputSlot, waitForPreparedSlot, and endProblem that make the intended order obvious.
Research: The refactor note recommends these seams so tests no longer have to mix listener and service APIs manually.

title: Add cancelAsyncReset to BatchPointerReset test
description:
Background: Production main.cpp calls cancelAsyncReset after preProblem to clear ring state before the next problem.
Motivation: The current test skips that reset, so stale ring state can hide the very regression the test is meant to catch.
Goal: Mirror the production boundary sequence so the test exercises the same problem-switch behavior.
Research: The branch review says the test currently passes only because it never drives beginAsyncReset plus advanceBuffer.

title: Test ResetSubmissionHappensBeforePostSolutionOrNextPrepare
description:
Background: The ring reset has to happen at the intended point in the solution flow, not after validation or after the next prepare step.
Motivation: Wrong ordering weakens the pipeline and can hide the real production bug even if the reset call eventually occurs.
Goal: Add a scheduler test that checks reset submission order relative to post-solution and the next prepare call.
Research: The test investigation says ordering is part of the missing regression guard, not just call count.

title: Coordinate scheduler-order coverage for the ring-reset seam
description:
Background: The production bug lives in main.cpp scheduling and call-site order, not in the DataInitialization internals.
Motivation: We need an umbrella for the scheduler seam so the concrete positive and negative path tests do not each re-specify the hook behavior.
Goal: Define the spy/reset-sink seam, verify no-benchmark submits two resets after warmup and benchmark mode bypasses the hook, and keep the path-specific assertions in ndi and ve2.
Research: This bead coordinates the scheduler-order coverage only; it should not duplicate the implementation logic owned by the canonical path tests.

title: Separate slot storage from slot arithmetic
description:
Background: The ring path currently spreads active-slot state across gpuInput.current, gpuInput.batch, m_gpuPtrs, m_gpuBatchPtrs, m_cachedGPUInputs, m_gpuPtrsRing, and m_gpuBatchPtrsRing.
Motivation: advanceBuffer has to mutate several aliases at once, and SlotGuard exists only because storage and activation are interleaved.
Goal: Introduce a slot repository or GpuInputSlotSet so activation and storage are managed in one place.
Research: The refactor note says this seam is what makes slot identity testable without HIP allocations.

title: Track residual DataInitialization cleanup
description:
Background: The proposal says 18n and uer own the explicit call-site comment and shared tensor-population helper work.
Motivation: This bead should hold only the remaining cleanup nits so it does not compete with those canonical owners.
Goal: Track whatever residual DataInitialization cleanup remains after 18n and uer land, and keep the scope limited to non-overlapping nits.
Research: The proposal explicitly says h8p should retain only cleanup work that is not already owned by 18n or uer.

title: Test PristineOnGpuFalseDisablesWarmD2DReset
description:
Background: The warm-path D2D reset only works when the pristine copy exists on the GPU.
Motivation: If pristine copies are not kept on the GPU, a warm D2D reset would read from an uninitialized or stale source buffer.
Goal: Add a test that proves the ring becomes ineligible when --pristine-on-gpu is false.
Research: The proposal explicitly requires m_keepPristineCopyOnGPU as part of ring eligibility.

title: Add makeBatchedProblem shared test helper
description:
Background: The stale-alt-slot regression relies on two batched problems with different strides so stale pointers are obvious.
Motivation: The problem setup should live in one helper instead of being duplicated inline in the integration test.
Goal: Add a helper that constructs the batched problem variants used to prove the ring refreshes pointers after a problem switch.
Research: The test investigation uses makeBatchedProblem for the p1-to-p2 stale-pointer coverage.

title: Add makePlainProblem shared test helper
description:
Background: Several ring-buffer tests need a simple non-batched GEMM problem with stable slot identity.
Motivation: Re-creating the same plain problem in each test makes the pointer-rotation checks noisy and repetitive.
Goal: Add a helper that builds the plain problem shape used by the slot-rotation tests.
Research: The test plan explicitly calls out makePlainProblem as a reusable fixture for the fast-path and scheduling tests.

title: Test WarmRingValidationPathResetsOutputsBeforeReuse
description:
Background: The warm ring path currently skips output reset on the assumption that a slot was once pristine.
Motivation: That assumption stops being valid after a slot has already been used by a kernel and must be revalidated.
Goal: Add a GPU integration test that dirties a slot, reuses it through the warm path, and verifies the output tensors were reset before reuse.
Research: Proposal 1 in the ring-buffer proposal document describes this as the key validation-sensitive warm-path behavior.

title: Reset m_batchInit inside cancelAsyncReset
description:
Background: The review found that cancelAsyncReset resets ring indices and slot maps, but it does not clear m_batchInit.
Motivation: Today the code only stays correct because preProblem always runs first; if the call order changes or cancelAsyncReset is called alone, batch pointers can stay stale for the next problem.
Goal: Make the freshness reset self-contained by clearing m_batchInit in cancelAsyncReset, not only in preProblem.
Research: The branch review calls this a hidden ordering dependency and notes that the existing fix lives only in preProblem.

title: Test CancelResetsToSlotZero
description:
Background: cancelAsyncReset is supposed to restore the ring to a clean problem-boundary state.
Motivation: If cancel leaves the active slot or pending availability dirty, the next problem can inherit stale ring state.
Goal: Add a unit test that proves cancel returns the controller to slot zero and clears pending work.
Research: The proposed state-machine tests explicitly call out CancelResetsToSlotZero.

title: Add a production scheduler test for no-benchmark ring resets
description:
Background: The production scheduler bug is the no-benchmark call-site, not DataInitialization itself.
Motivation: We need one canonical no-benchmark scheduler regression that owns the spy/reset-sink seam and the real client call order.
Goal: Add a spy-based scheduler test that confirms two resets are submitted in no-benchmark mode, none are submitted on the benchmark path, and reset submission happens before the next prepare step.
Research: This is the canonical home for the 71o duplicate and must follow the sah policy anchor.

title: Audit and harden proxy predicates in input initialization
description:
Background: The architectural-principle note calls out Proxy Predicate as the pattern where a cheap flag is read as if it meant a broader invariant.
Motivation: m_batchInit, the CPU input fast-path condition, and the preSolution MX refresh check all rely on proxy state that can drift from the true precondition.
Goal: Centralize or assert the full predicate so batch-pointer freshness, CPU fast-path eligibility, and MX re-init consistency are explicit instead of implied.
Research: The note explicitly lists those three sites as the high-confidence and medium-confidence examples to investigate.

title: Add a stale-alt-slot refresh integration test
description:
Background: cancelAsyncReset should prevent slot-1 data from problem p1 from leaking into p2.
Motivation: This is the observable regression the batch-pointer bug exposed in the first place.
Goal: Switch problems, re-prime, advance into the new alt slot, and verify the batch pointers reflect p2 rather than stale p1 strides.
Research: The test plan uses different batched strides for p1 and p2 so the stale-data failure is obvious.

title: Add buildBaseDataInitArgs shared test helper
description:
Background: The test plan calls for a shared builder that creates the base po::variables_map used by the DataInit regression tests.
Motivation: Rebuilding the full CLI option map in every test makes the ring-buffer and batch-pointer cases fragile and hard to read.
Goal: Provide one helper that seeds the common DataInitialization arguments so focused tests only override the field under test.
Research: The investigation note lists buildBaseDataInitArgs as the first shared fixture to extract.

title: Separate rotating-output and I-cache rotation policy from the core run loop
description:
Background: The client currently mixes ring-buffer slots, rotating output or input buffers, and I-cache code-object rotation in adjacent main.cpp code.
Motivation: That coupling makes ring-buffer reasoning harder and ties unrelated rotation policies together.
Goal: Extract a rotating-input planner and an I-cache rotation policy so the core run loop only coordinates execution.
Research: The note says those decisions should become pure unit-testable policy objects.

title: Thread the copy stream through NaN-mode output reset
description:
Background: resetOutput only takes the async path in the non-NaN branch; the NaN path falls back to synchronous copies through copyBadInputBuffers and CopyTensorVoid.
Motivation: That blocks the CPU even when a copy stream exists, so the ring path loses overlap in validation-heavy modes.
Goal: Pass the target stream through the NaN path so the output reset can stay asynchronous when the copy kind allows it.
Research: The branch review marks this as degraded async behavior, not a correctness corruption bug.

title: Test BenchmarkModeDoesNotUseNoBenchmarkResetHook
description:
Background: The no-benchmark reset hook is only intended for the untimed validation-driven path.
Motivation: Benchmark mode should not submit extra resets that change the measured behavior.
Goal: Add a test that proves benchmark mode does not take the no-benchmark ring-reset hook.
Research: The proposal and scheduler notes both call this out as an explicit negative case.

title: Coordinate shared DataInit test fixtures
description:
Background: The DataInit regression tests need shared setup helpers so individual cases stay focused.
Motivation: Rebuilding the long option maps and HIP stream ownership in every test makes the ring-buffer cases brittle and noisy.
Goal: Own the helper layer for buildBaseDataInitArgs, buildRingArgs, makePlainProblem, makeBatchedProblem, and HipStreamGuard.
Research: This bead is the helper umbrella; typed DataInitConfig ownership belongs in 0b1.

title: Roll back partial alt-buffer allocations on failure
description:
Background: When alt-buffer allocation fails partway through, DataInitialization leaves earlier allocations alive in the object even after m_hasAltBuffers is cleared.
Motivation: Under memory pressure those partially allocated buffers can consume device memory for the life of the client and trigger avoidable OOMs later.
Goal: Either free already-created alt allocations on failure or use a guard that rolls back the partial state automatically.
Research: The review calls this a plausible partial-allocation leak in allocNewGPUInputs.

title: Add an assertion or comment for the grouped GEMM fast path bypass
description:
Background: The async-ring fast path skips some grouped-GEMM-specific dispatch checks in the current implementation.
Motivation: That behavior may be correct today, but it is easy to misread as an accidental omission when the code is scanned later.
Goal: Add a short assertion or comment that explains why the grouped-GEMM fast path is safe, or make the bypass explicit if it is not.
Research: The branch review lists this as a minor maintainability note rather than a correctness bug.

title: Clarify the warm-path D overwrite comment
description:
Background: The warm-path comment says D is completely overwritten, but that statement is only true under the intended preconditions.
Motivation: A future reader can mistake the comment for a universal invariant and miss the validation-sensitive case.
Goal: Rewrite the comment so it states the exact precondition for skipping the reset work.
Research: The branch review flags this comment as misleading but not currently incorrect under the intended GEMM path.

title: Make ring enablement explicit and allocation-aware
description:
Background: Proposal 2 separates timed benchmark enqueues, validation-driven untimed runs, and physical ring allocation, and this bead is the source of truth for that split.
Motivation: The current m_numActiveBuffers choice and allocation loop conflate those modes, so the code allocates or indexes slots that are not actually usable.
Goal: Add an explicit m_ringAllowed policy, size m_numActiveBuffers from that policy, and allocate alt buffers only up to the active ring size.
Research: Timed benchmark runs should not allocate or consume the ring, validation-only runs should use three slots, and zero-enqueue/no-validation runs should not claim warm ring behavior. This policy supersedes w5n and is the canonical ring-enable source of truth.

title: Test AdvanceWrapsModuloActiveBufferCount
description:
Background: Triple-buffer mode should rotate slot 2 back to slot 0.
Motivation: The wraparound behavior is easy to get wrong when slot arithmetic is embedded in the client runtime.
Goal: Add a unit test that proves the active index wraps correctly across the configured buffer count.
Research: The investigation note names AdvanceWrapsModuloActiveBufferCount as one of the explicit state-machine checks.

title: Test ZeroEnqueueNoValidationConfigurationDoesNotClaimWarmRingBehavior
description:
Background: With zero benchmark enqueues and no validation or printing, the solution loop should not be driving ring behavior.
Motivation: The code should not pretend that warm-ring behavior exists in a mode where no listener keeps the loop alive.
Goal: Add a test that proves the zero-enqueue, no-validation configuration does not run the ring path.
Research: The proposal notes that this mode should not claim warm ring behavior at all.

title: Split copy planning from copy execution
description:
Background: copyInputs and resetOutput both decide source and destination, choose copy kind, and mutate the caller-owned views.
Motivation: fillSlot has to work around that mutation behavior, which makes the flow fragile.
Goal: Add a pure copy-plan layer and execute it through the copy engine, or at minimum rename the current routines so their intent is explicit during migration.
Research: The refactor note recommends a TensorCopyOp plan plus a separate executor.

title: Make swizzle uploads stream-aware
description:
Background: fillSlot calls copySwizzledToGPUBuffer, but that helper routes its host-to-device copies through the default/null stream.
Motivation: That blocks CPU overlap and weakens the ordering guarantees around the async ring path.
Goal: Thread the copy stream through the swizzle path and record the copy-done event on the same stream.
Research: The review flags this as a medium-severity async regression in copySwizzledToGPUBuffer.

title: Extract a shared populateTensorSlot helper for fillSlot and prepareGPUInputsInternal
description:
Background: fillSlot and prepareGPUInputsInternal both run the same tensor-population sequence, but the slow path also includes a rotating-buffer block that fillSlot does not mirror.
Motivation: Duplicated population logic is a maintenance risk because future changes can land in one path and not the other.
Goal: Extract a shared helper that populates tensor slots and makes the rotating-buffer behavior explicit.
Research: The branch review calls the divergence between the two functions a cleanup opportunity, not a correctness bug today.

title: Test BenchmarkPathDoesNotUseNoBenchmarkResetHook
description:
Background: Proposal 2's scheduler seam says benchmark mode must bypass the no-benchmark ring-reset hook.
Motivation: The benchmark-path negative case is the canonical guard that keeps the timing path from inheriting no-benchmark behavior.
Goal: Verify the reset sink is never invoked on the benchmark path and keep this bead as the owner of that negative regression.
Research: This subsumes pfz. The behavior must stay consistent with sah's explicit ring-enable policy.

title: Move MX and swizzle logic behind a policy object
description:
Background: MX scale and swizzle decisions depend on architecture, problem shape, user options, and selected solution.
Motivation: The current logic depends on ambient state from preSolution, which makes ring slots and copy paths sensitive to hidden context.
Goal: Compute a copy or layout plan from explicit inputs instead of mutating DataInitialization based on the current solution.
Research: The refactor note suggests an MxInputSpecializer or MxScaleLayoutPolicy for this.

title: Correct buffering mode selection when benchmarks are disabled
description:
Background: The constructor currently sets m_numActiveBuffers with noBenchmarkRuns ? 3 : 2.
Motivation: No-benchmark mode never enters the benchmark loop, so triple buffering is idle there while benchmark mode gets the shallower pipeline.
Goal: Use the correct buffer-depth mapping so the active ring matches the actual execution mode.
Research: The branch review says the assignment is inverted and should be noBenchmarkRuns ? 2 : 3.

title: Test Slot2NotAllocatedWhenActiveRingSizeIsOne
description:
Background: Proposal 2 separates physical allocation from ring policy and says slot allocation should follow the active ring size.
Motivation: Allocating unused slot 2 in disabled-ring mode wastes memory and hides the real policy boundary.
Goal: Add a test that proves slot 2 is not allocated when m_numActiveBuffers is 1.
Research: The proposal calls this out as the allocation check that matches the new ring policy.

title: Test MarkBarrierWaitedClearsBarrier
description:
Background: Once the compute stream is told to wait on the copy-done event, the pending barrier should be cleared.
Motivation: A stale barrier flag would make the scheduler think the slot still needs synchronization and could suppress later transitions.
Goal: Add a unit test that proves the wait step clears the barrier-needed state.
Research: The investigation note lists MarkBarrierWaitedClearsBarrier as part of the ring-state contract.

title: Add RingSlotController state-machine tests
description:
Background: The test plan proposes extracting ring-slot accounting into a HIP-free controller before writing more GPU-heavy tests.
Motivation: Slot priming, advancement, wrapping, barrier state, and cancel behavior should be proven without device code.
Goal: Add state-machine tests for PrimeDoesNotOverfill, AdvanceConsumesAvailableSlot, AdvanceWrapsModuloActiveBufferCount, AdvanceMarksCopyBarrierRequired, MarkBarrierWaitedClearsBarrier, and CancelResetsToSlotZero.
Research: The investigation note lists those exact cases as the desired unit coverage for the extracted controller.

title: Test AdvanceConsumesAvailableSlot
description:
Background: A primed slot should be consumed when the active buffer advances.
Motivation: If advance does not decrement availability, the ring state machine can hand out the same slot twice.
Goal: Add a unit test that verifies advancing the ring updates the active index and reduces the available-slot count.
Research: The proposed controller tests include AdvanceConsumesAvailableSlot as a required transition.

title: Add a fast-path distinct-valid-alt-slot integration test
description:
Background: A primed ring slot should rotate to a distinct alt allocation and still contain valid initialized data.
Motivation: Pointer inequality alone can miss slot-rotation failures, and readback alone can miss identity mistakes.
Goal: Verify that prepareGPUInputs returns a different pointer after priming and that the returned alt slot reads back the expected tensor contents.
Research: The test-investigation note gives a concrete p1-style sketch for this path.

title: Test BoundsCheckDoesNotPrimeRing
description:
Background: The ring fast path is only eligible when bounds checking is disabled.
Motivation: Any other bounds-check mode should keep the client on the conservative path.
Goal: Add a negative test that proves beginAsyncReset does not enable ring advancement when bounds checking is on.
Research: The investigation note lists bounds-check gating as one of the minimal negative guards to keep.
